en.title: Carolina goes for a Helsinki sweep with Aho on a roll at home
en.deck: Carolina beat Seattle 4-1 on Thursday in the first Global Series game in Helsinki. Finnish star Sebastian Aho scored twice and the Hurricanes outshot the Kraken 30-13. The rematch at Veikkaus Arena starts at 1 p.m. ET, and the model makes Carolina a clear favourite, though not quite as big a one as the market does.
news: Brandon Bussi played Thursday, so Pyotr Kochetkov (11-1-0, .920) is projected to start for Carolina. Seattle is expected to go to Joey Daccord after Philipp Grubauer made 26 saves in the opener. Neither starter is confirmed.
Jordan Staal (calf) has practised on the trip, and Rod Brind'Amour called him a game-time decision.
Seattle is without Jared McCann (lower body). Coach Lane Lambert is not sure Ryan Lindgren will be ready on this trip.
Kaapo Kakko, who grew up in Turku, has 13 points in 16 games and said he had been waiting all season for this trip.
records: Carolina (15-3-2) has won three straight and seven of its last eight.
Aho has three straight multipoint games (3 goals, 4 assists). Jackson Blake has a 10-game point streak and Logan Stankoven a six-game streak.
Taylor Hall played his 1,000th NHL game on Thursday, the first player to reach that mark outside North America.
Seattle has lost three of four and allowed 3.8 goals a game over its last five.
betting: Market: Hurricanes 1.26, Kraken 4.00, about 76–24 without the margin. The model has Carolina at 70%, so it gives Seattle a little more of a chance than the market.
Total: over 5.5 at 1.62 is about 59%, exactly the model's number. The last seven meetings, including Thursday's 4-1, averaged 5.7 goals.
Player chances (model): Aho 1+ point 69% and goal 38% (market about 40%). Brandon Montour 1+ point 39% against roughly 34% in the market, and K'Andre Miller 1+ point 39% against about 33%.

en.title: Scheifele needs one point to own the Jets' scoring record

Patrick Kane returned for Chicago on Thursday after missing three games with an upper-body injury. Ryan Donato scored the overtime winner and Frank Nazar scored twice.
Spencer Knight (21 saves Thursday) is expected in the Chicago net.
records: Scheifele's next point breaks the Jets/Thrashers franchise record.
Dawson Mercer has scored twice in each of his last two games.

Sturm called Thursday's game very flat and shuffled his defence pairs at Friday's practice.
records: Kirill Kaprizov (6 goals, 12 assists) and Quinn Hughes both have 10-game point streaks.

Morgan Rielly is day-to-day with a lower-body injury from Nov. 7.
Edmonton beat Philadelphia 3-2 in overtime on Wednesday on Evan Bouchard's winner, with two goals from Zach Hyman.
records: McDavid (11 goals, 38 assists) is the fourth player with a point in each of a season's first 20 games, after Wayne Gretzky, Mats Sundin and Dany Heatley.
Leon Draisaitl has a seven-game point streak (6 goals, 7 assists).

en.title: Hot Devils finish the home-and-home in Washington
